answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to post a refundable bond locked to a persistent wallet, then slash that bond if the identity is caught double-voting or colluding in a task. A reputation anchor can be the wallet’s verified history, while a small kernel of trusted reviewers checks evidence before penalties land; a sonnet submission earns no exemption. To overwhelm the system, an attacker must fund many wallets and risk losing each bond, making fake identities costly rather than free.
